title: Austin: New Traffic Rules, Corporate Taxes, & Paving
summary:
*   **New Traffic Rules and Business Sign Permit:** The city updated its traffic regulations and approved an electric light sign for Wimbisch Drug Company at 308 Congress Avenue, detailing specific design requirements.
*   **Aggressive Tax Collection Strategy:** To boost city revenue, officials hired attorneys on a 20% contingency fee to collect overdue and future municipal taxes from corporations on securities held by the state for the years 1916-1918.
*   **Major Infrastructure Development:** The city accepted new paving work on Rio Grande Street (19th to 28th), approved funding for multiple new sanitary sewer lines, and allocated funds for engineering fees for the Waller Creek Bridge on East 19th Street.
*   **Key Financial Approvals:** The 1916 tax rolls, totaling over $468,000, were officially approved. Additionally, $5,000 was transferred from the Water, Light, and Power Department's surplus to support the Sanitary Sewer fund.

The State of Texas
County of Travis.

Whereas, it is the desire of the City of Austin to enforce the collec-tion of all taxes
due by domestic Corporations on securities owned by them and on depos- -its in the
Treasury of the State of Texas for all years for which same are legally taxable; and,
Whereas, it will be necessary ,in order to determine whether such securities are taxab-ble
,for the City to have instituted and prosecuted certain test suits for the enforcement and
collection of such taxes, which suit or suits will probable not be finally determined
until at least during the year of 1918; and, Whereas, pending the final determination of
such suit or suits, taxes on such securities by such domestic Corporations for the years
1916,1917, and 1918 will in all probability have become due and owing to the City of
Austin; and, Whereas, it is the desire of the City of Austin to retain and employ J W
Maxwelland the firm of Lightfoot, Brady & Robertson ,Attorneys at Law, for the purpose of
instituting and prosecuting to final determination of such suit or suits, and the
collection of all such taxes for said years; now, therefore, This contract made and
entered into on this date by and between the City of Austin, a municipal Corporation
,acting by A P Wooldridge, its Mayor, who is duly authorized to execute this contract by
resolution duly passed by the City Council ,as party of the first part ,and J W Maxwell
and Lightfoot, Brady & Robertson ,as parties of the second part, Witnesseth : 1. The
parties of the second part hereby agree and bind themselves to prepare and compile or
cause to be prepared and compiled a correct list of all such personal property and
securities owned by all such domestic Corporations on deposits with the State Treasurer in
the State Treasury of the State of Texas for and during the years 1916, 1917 and 1918, and
to forward such lists to the party of the first part ,and in case any such unrendered
property and securities have not theretofore been legally assessed for taxes by said City
for said years 1916,1917 and 1918. to furnish said party of the first part, and the proper
Officers thereof, with all of such data and information as will enable said party of the
first part and its Officers to make a legal assessment thereof for taxes for the years
1916,1917 and 1918,and to furnish said party of the first part with data and information
showing that such property and securities are legally taxable by the City under the laws
of this State and under the Judgement and decisions of the Courts in said test case or
cases before mentioned; and to receive and collect all such taxes ,interest and penalties
on such property and securities aforesaid for the years 1916,1917 and 1918, whether
heretofore or hereafter assessed; and to bring and diligently execute all suits that may
be necessary to enforce the payment of all such taxes, interest and penalties thereon,
whether the same are now due and delinquent or may be hereafter become due and delinquent
for the years 1916,1917 and 1918, and to do and perform all other things necessary and
proper to be done in the collection of all such taxes. interest and penalties.
2. That in consideration of the services heretofore performed by parties of the second
part and of those hereafter to be performed by them ,as herein provided, the said party of
the first part hereby agrees and binds itself to pay to the said parties of the second
part a fee and compensation of twenty per cent (20%) of all such taxes, interest and
penal-ties, which shall be collected and received by said party of the first part;
